chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ubaydullah al-Dihqan, from Durust, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The most perfect of the people in intellect is the best of them in morals.'

key_terms.خُلُق: Khuluq — moral character, innate disposition, ethics; plural akhlaq
key_terms.عقل: 'Aql — intellect, reason; in Shia theology, a faculty that encompasses both cognitive and moral dimensions

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the relationship between intellect and morals?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a profound link between intellectual perfection and moral excellence, teaching that a person's true rational completeness is measured by the goodness of their character. This hadith was transmitted through a chain of six narrators including Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi and Durust ibn Abi Mansur. In the Shia tradition, this teaching reflects the Imams' emphasis that 'aql (intellect) is not merely cognitive ability but is deeply intertwined with ethical conduct — a person who behaves with the finest morals demonstrates the highest form of rational development.
